type block = interface { fn block_size() usize; fn encrypt_block([]u8, []u8) void;
	fn decrypt_block([]u8, []u8) void; }                   // aes, des, des3
	fn cbc_encrypt[B: block](b: *B, iv: []u8, data: []u8) (void | bad_length)  // and cbc_decrypt
	fn ctr_new[B: block](b: B, iv: []u8) (stream[B] | bad_length)
	fn cfb_encrypter, cfb_decrypter, ofb_new[B: block](b: B, iv: []u8) (stream[B] | bad_length)
	fn xor_stream[B](s: *stream[B], data: []u8) void;  fn stream_wipe[B](s: *stream[B]) void
	fn x25519(scalar: *[32]u8, point: *[32]u8) [32]u8;  fn x25519_public(private: *[32]u8) [32]u8
	fn ed25519_generate() ed25519_private;  fn ed25519_from_seed(seed: *[32]u8) ed25519_private
	fn ed25519_public(k) [32]u8;  fn ed25519_seed(k) [32]u8;  fn ed25519_wipe(k) void
	fn ed25519_private_bytes(k) [64]u8;  fn ed25519_from_bytes(b: *[64]u8) (ed25519_private | bad_key_bytes)
	fn ed25519_sign(k, msg: []u8) [64]u8;  fn ed25519_verify(public: *[32]u8, msg, sig) (void | bad_signature)
	fn ed25519_sign_with(k, msg, opts: *ed25519_options) ([64]u8 | bad_context)   // ctx and ph
	fn ed25519_verify_with(public, msg, sig, opts: *ed25519_options) (void | bad_signature)
type ed25519_options = struct { context: []u8, prehashed: bool }
type curve = enum { p256, p384, p521 };  fn curve_bytes(c: curve) usize   // 32, 48, 66
	fn ec_generate(c: curve) ec_private;  fn ec_private_from(c, d: []u8) (ec_private | bad_scalar)
	fn ec_private_bytes(k, out: []u8) []u8;  fn ec_public_bytes(k, out: []u8) []u8   // 0x04 || x || y
	fn ec_public_of(k: *ec_private) ec_public;  fn ec_public_from(c, b: []u8) (ec_public | bad_point)
	fn ecdh(k: *ec_private, peer: []u8, out: []u8) ([]u8 | bad_point)
	fn ecdsa_sign(key, h: hash_kind, digest, out: []u8) []u8          // r || s, RFC 6979 nonces
	fn ecdsa_sign_asn1(key, h, digest, out: []u8) []u8               // DER, at most 139 bytes
	fn ecdsa_verify(k: *ec_public, digest: []u8, r: *nat, s: *nat) (void | bad_signature)
	fn ecdsa_verify_asn1(k: *ec_public, digest: []u8, sig: []u8) (void | bad_signature)
	fn rsa_generate(bits: usize) (rsa_private | bad_key_size)       // 2048 to 4096, e = 65537
	fn rsa_private_from(n, e, d, p, q: []u8) (rsa_private | bad_rsa_key)   // checked
	fn rsa_private_parts(k, out: *[8][512]u8) [8]usize   // n e d p q dp dq qinv, big-endian
	fn rsa_public_of(k: *rsa_private) rsa_public
	fn rsa_sign_pkcs1, rsa_sign_pss(k: *rsa_private, h, digest, out: []u8) ([]u8 | bad_key_size | bad_signature)
	fn rsa_verify_pkcs1(k: *rsa_public, h: hash_kind, digest: []u8, sig: []u8) (void | bad_signature)
	fn rsa_verify_pss(k: *rsa_public, h: hash_kind, digest: []u8, sig: []u8) (void | bad_signature)
	fn rsa_encrypt_oaep(k: *rsa_public, h, label, msg, out: []u8) ([]u8 | too_long_for_key)
	fn rsa_decrypt_oaep(k: *rsa_private, h, label, ct, out: []u8) ([]u8 | decrypt_error)
	fn rsa_encrypt_pkcs1(k: *rsa_public, msg, out: []u8) ([]u8 | too_long_for_key)
	fn rsa_decrypt_pkcs1(k: *rsa_private, ct, out: []u8) ([]u8 | decrypt_error)
	fn rsa_decrypt_pkcs1_key(k: *rsa_private, ct, key: []u8) (void | decrypt_error)  // session keys
type dsa_sizes = enum u8 { l1024_n160, l2048_n224, l2048_n256, l3072_n256 }
	fn dsa_generate_params(s: dsa_sizes) dsa_params;  fn dsa_generate_key(d: *dsa_params) (dsa_private | bad_dsa)
	fn dsa_public_from(p, q, g, y: []u8) (dsa_public | bad_dsa);  fn dsa_private_from(p, q, g, y, x) ...
	fn dsa_sign(k, h, digest, out: []u8) []u8;  fn dsa_sign_asn1(k, h, digest, out: []u8) []u8
	fn dsa_verify(k: *dsa_public, digest, r: *nat, s: *nat) (void | bad_signature);  fn dsa_verify_asn1(...)
	fn dsa_public_of(k) dsa_public;  fn dsa_wipe(k) void
type mlkem_level = enum u8 { mlkem512, mlkem768, mlkem1024 }
	fn mlkem_generate(l: mlkem_level) mlkem_private;  fn mlkem_from_seed(l, seed: *[64]u8) mlkem_private
	fn mlkem_public_of(k) mlkem_public;  fn mlkem_public_bytes(k, out: []u8) []u8
	fn mlkem_public_from(l, b: []u8) (mlkem_public | bad_mlkem_key);  fn mlkem_seed(k) [64]u8
	fn mlkem_encapsulate(k: *mlkem_public, ct: []u8) [32]u8               // the secret; ct to send
	fn mlkem_decapsulate(k: *mlkem_private, ct: []u8) ([32]u8 | bad_ciphertext)
	fn mlkem_sizes(l) (usize, usize, usize);  fn mlkem_private_bytes(k, out) []u8;  fn mlkem_wipe(k) void
	fn random(buf: []u8) void                     // the system's CSPRNG
	fn random_below(n: u64) u64;  fn random_text() [26]u8   // base 32, 128 bits
	fn equal(a: []u8, b: []u8) bool               // constant time, as are these:
	fn byte_eq(x, y: u8) u8;  fn eq32(x, y: u32) u32;  fn less_or_eq32(x, y: u32) u32
	fn select(v, x, y: u8) u8;  fn copy_if(v: u8, dst: []u8, src: []u8) void
	fn xor(dst: []u8, a: []u8, b: []u8) usize
	fn wipe(b: []u8) void

Sealing encrypts data in place and gives the tag; opening checks the tag before it decrypts, and leaves data as it was when the tag is wrong.

SHA-3 and SHAKE are Keccak (FIPS 202), and cSHAKE adds a function name and customization string (SP 800-185). A SHAKE reads out as many bytes as wanted; once read, it takes no more writes. BLAKE2b and BLAKE2s (RFC 7693) take a key, salt and personalization, and every hash here works through the one hash interface, so HMAC, HKDF and PBKDF2 take them all.

Ed25519 (RFC 8032) signs deterministically. Verification refuses an S that is not reduced and a public key that is not encoded canonically, so a signature has one form only. ed25519_options gives Ed25519ctx (a context of up to 255 bytes) and Ed25519ph (the message's SHA-512 digest signed in its place).

ECDSA's nonces are RFC 6979's, made from the key and digest, so signing needs no randomness. P-521's points and scalars are 66 bytes, and its signatures in DER at most 139. Keys and ECDH work in constant time on all three curves. RSA keys are 2048 to 4096 bits:

  • rsa_generate sieves 2048 odd numbers at a time by the primes below 2¹⁶, and tests what is left by Miller–Rabin in constant time: a 2048-bit key takes about 50 ms, a 4096-bit one about half a second.
  • Montgomery multiplication, nearly all the time of RSA and the curves, is the runtime's assembly (arm64 and x86-64), on 64-bit limbs where the modulus has an even number of 32-bit ones: a 2048-bit signature takes 1.5 ms.
  • A key with its primes signs and decrypts by the CRT, four times faster than with d alone.
  • Every private operation is checked with the public key before its result is given.
  • OAEP decryption makes all its checks in constant time.
  • PKCS #1 v1.5 decryption is for old protocols: how it fails can tell an attacker something, which rsa_decrypt_pkcs1_key avoids for session keys.

ML-KEM (FIPS 203) agrees on a 32-byte secret that a quantum computer cannot recover. One side encapsulates to the other's public key and sends the ciphertext; the other decapsulates it. A ciphertext that was not made for the key gives a secret no one else has, rather than an error, so how decapsulation fails says nothing about the key. A key is kept as its 64-byte seed. ML-KEM-768 is the usual choice, and nothing in its arithmetic on secrets divides or branches.

XChaCha20-Poly1305, and NaCl's secretbox and box, take 24-byte nonces, long enough to choose at random. A box is sealed with the shared key of two X25519 keys, so it shows who sealed it. A sealed box from box_seal_anonymous comes from a key made for it alone, so it shows nothing of the sender.

Passwords are kept as Argon2id, scrypt or bcrypt hashes, each slow and salted on purpose:

  • Argon2id (RFC 9106) is for new work. Its time, memory and lanes set the cost; argon2 also gives Argon2i and Argon2d, with a secret key and associated data.
  • scrypt (RFC 7914) costs 128·n·r bytes of memory.
  • bcrypt writes the $2b$ form, reads $2a$, $2b$ and $2y$, and refuses a password of more than 72 bytes rather than cut it. Its Blowfish reads tables by secret indices, as every bcrypt does, so it is not constant time.

DSA (FIPS 186-4) and RC4 are for keys and data old systems made. DSA is withdrawn from FIPS 186-5, and its signatures here take RFC 6979's nonces, so signing needs no randomness. A domain from outside is checked: its sizes, q dividing p − 1, and g of order q. RC4's output can be told from random, and its table is read at secret indices.

CBC, CTR, CFB and OFB work over any block. None of them authenticates, so pair them with a MAC, or use GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305. CBC keeps iv as the last ciphertext block, so a message can be done in parts. DES and triple DES are for reading what old systems wrote: DES falls to search, and both have a 64-bit block. Their S-boxes are read whole, like AES's fallback, so the time they take says nothing of the key.

x509 — certificates

lora 
fn parse(der: []u8) (cert | invalid)          // views of der
	fn pem_certs(text: []u8) (^[]^[]u8 | invalid | nomem)
	fn pool_from_file(path: str) (pool | invalid | fs::error | nomem)
	fn system_roots() (pool | invalid | fs::error | nomem)  // /etc/ssl/cert.pem
	fn verify(chain: []cert, roots: *pool, host: str, now: i64) (void | invalid | nomem)
	fn for_host(c: *cert, host: str) bool

verify checks each signature up to a root in the pool, the dates, the issuers' basic constraints and key usage, the leaf's extended key usage, and, when host is not "", that the leaf is for it: a DNS name (one leading *. label as a wildcard) or an IPv4 or IPv6 address. A critical extension it does not know is refused. Keys: RSA, ECDSA P-256 and P-384.

tls — TLS 1.3 clients and servers

lora 
type config = struct {
	server_name: str = "",       // SNI, and the name verified
	verify: verify_mode = verify_mode::full,  // full, chain (no name), none
	roots: nullable *const x509::pool = null, // null: the system's
	alpn: str = "",                           // "h2,http/1.1": best first
	cert_chain: []const []const u8 = [],      // ours, leaf first, DER
	cert_key: nullable *const x509::private_key = null,
}
type error = !(alert | failed | x509::invalid | coro::error);

fn client(fd: int, cfg: *config) (conn | error | nomem)  // over a connected socket
fn client_on(s: *const net::conn, cfg: *config) (conn | error | nomem)  // keeps to s's deadlines
	fn read(c: *conn, buf: []u8) (usize | error | nomem)      // 0 at the end
	fn write(c: *conn, data: []u8) (void | error | nomem)
	fn close(c: *conn) void                                   // close_notify; the socket stays
	fn set_deadline(c: *conn, by: u64) void                   // reads and writes stop waiting then
	fn negotiated(c: *conn) str                               // the ALPN protocol chosen
	fn server_end_point(c: *conn) []u8                        // RFC 5929, for channel binding

X25519 key exchange, or P-256 or P-384 for a server that asks for one (HelloRetryRequest); ChaCha20-Poly1305 (offered first), AES-128-GCM and AES-256-GCM; the server's chain verified, its CertificateVerify (ECDSA, RSA-PSS) and Finished checked; KeyUpdate followed. A server that asks for a certificate gets ours, signed with ECDSA or RSA-PSS, when the config has one. tls::version(&c) says which was spoken.

A server that speaks no later than TLS 1.2 is spoken to so: ECDHE with ECDSA or RSA certificates and the same three AEADs, the extended master secret required (RFC 7627), renegotiation refused, and a fall back from TLS 1.3 that someone between made refused. TLS 1.1 and older, static RSA key exchange and CBC ciphers are not spoken.

Servers. server and server_on answer a client with TLS 1.3 only. A client that offers nothing later than TLS 1.2 is refused with a protocol_version alert.

  • Key exchange: X25519, P-256 or P-384, the client's share taken if it sent one of those. Otherwise a HelloRetryRequest asks for the best of them it supports.
  • Cipher suite: the client's first choice of the three.
  • Signing: the certificate's key signs with ECDSA (P-256 or P-384) or RSA-PSS, as the client accepts.
  • ALPN: the server's protocols, best first; the first one the client also offers is chosen. A client that offers only others is refused with a no_application_protocol alert.
  • Client certificates: client_auth asks for them: request takes a connection without one, require refuses it. A certificate sent must lead to client_roots and be for authenticating clients. peer_certificate gives its DER.
  • Failures: sent to the client as the alert RFC 8446 names.

server_on and client_on keep to the socket's read and write deadlines (net::set_read_deadline, net::set_write_deadline) as they are each time they wait, so a server can change them between requests.

lora 
type server_config = struct {
	cert_chain: []const []const u8,          // leaf first, DER
	cert_key: *const x509::private_key,
	alpn: []const str = [],                  // best first
	client_auth: client_auth = client_auth::none,  // none, request, require
	client_roots: nullable *const x509::pool = null,  // null: the system's
}
fn server(fd: int, cfg: *const server_config) (conn | error | nomem)
fn server_on(s: *const net::conn, cfg: *const server_config) (conn | error | nomem)
	fn server_name(c: *const conn) str           // what the client asked for (SNI)
	fn peer_certificate(c: *const conn) []const u8  // the client's, DER; empty if none

kv — a key-value store, served and sharded

Values found by their keys, in memory for repeated access at low latency, and on disk if wanted: text, bytes, 64-bit integers and floats, JSON, lists of byte strings and sets of them. The store is split into shards by a keyed hash of the key, each with its own lock, so any number of threads and coroutines use one store at once through a *const store.

lora 
type options = struct { dir: str = "", residency: residency = residency::memory,
	sync: sync_policy = sync_policy::every_second, max_memory: u64 = 0,
	eviction: eviction = eviction::lru, shards: usize = 0,
	clock: nullable *thread::atomic = null }
type residency = enum u8 { memory, disk }            // disk: values in the log, keys in memory
type sync_policy = enum u8 { always, every_second, none }
type eviction = enum u8 { refuse, lru, random }     // at max_memory
type kind = enum u8 { text, bytes, integer, float, json, list, set }
type end = enum u8 { front, back }
type set_options = struct { ttl_ms: u64 = 0, only_new: bool = false,
	only_existing: bool = false, keep_ttl: bool = false }
type error = (wrong_kind | full | invalid_json | not_a_number | bad_log | fs::error | nomem)

fn open(opts: options) (store | error)              // its log, if it has one, read back
	fn close(s: *const store) (void | error)
	fn sync(s: *const store) (void | error);  fn compact(s: *const store) (void | error)
	fn count(s: *const store) usize;  fn memory_used(s: *const store) u64
	fn log_bytes(s: *const store) u64;  fn clear(s: *const store) (void | error)
	fn sweep(s: *const store, max: usize) usize      // expired keys, a shard at a time
	fn keys(s: *const store, out: *^[]^[]u8) (void | nomem)
fn set_text, set_int, set_float, set_json (s, key: str, value, o: set_options = ...) (bool | error)
	fn set_bytes(s, key: []const u8, value: []const u8, o: set_options = ...) (bool | error)
	fn get(s, key: str, out: *^[]u8) (kind | void | error)   // numbers as text
	fn get_bytes(s, key: []const u8, out: *^[]u8) (kind | void | error)
	fn get_int(s, key: str) (?i64 | error);  fn get_float(s, key: str) (?f64 | error)
	fn incr(s, key: str, n: i64 = 1) (i64 | error);  fn incr_float(s, key: str, x: f64) (f64 | error)
	fn append_text(s, key: str, more: str) (usize | error)
	fn remove(s, key: str) (bool | error);  fn remove_bytes(s, key: []const u8) (bool | error)
	fn exists(s, key: str) bool;  fn kind_of(s, key: str) ?kind
	fn expire(s, key: str, ttl_ms: u64) (bool | error);  fn persist(s, key: str) (bool | error)
	fn ttl(s, key: str) ?i64                          // ms left; -1: none
fn push_front, push_back (s, key: str, item: []const u8) (usize | error)
	fn pop_front, pop_back (s, key: str, out: *^[]u8) (bool | error)
	fn list_len(s, key: str) (usize | error)
	fn list_at(s, key: str, i: i64, out: *^[]u8) (bool | error)
	fn list_range(s, key: str, start: i64, stop: i64, out: *^[]^[]u8) (void | error)
fn set_add, set_remove, set_has (s, key: str, m: []const u8) (bool | error)
	fn set_len(s, key: str) (usize | error)
	fn set_members(s, key: str, out: *^[]^[]u8) (void | error)

// serving RESP, the protocol Redis clients speak
fn serve(s: *const store, l: *net::listener, stop: *thread::atomic,
	o: server_options = ...) (void | net::error)
	fn stop_serving(stop: *thread::atomic) void
type server_options = struct { max_request: usize = 64 << 20, max_args: usize = 1 << 16,
	request_ms: u64 = 10000, idle_ms: u64 = 0, password: str = "" }

// a client of one server
fn connect(to: net::address, o: client_options = ...) (client | remote_failure)
	fn call(c: *client, out: *reply, args: []const u8...) (void | remote_failure)
	fn remote_get(c, key, out: *^[]u8) (bool | remote_failure)
	fn remote_set(c, key, value, ttl_ms: u64 = 0) (void | remote_failure)
	fn remote_remove, remote_incr, remote_expire, remote_push_front, remote_push_back,
		remote_pop_front, remote_pop_back, remote_set_add, remote_set_has
type remote_failure = (refused | bad_reply | net::error | nomem)
type reply = struct { kind: reply_kind, num: i64, text: ^[]u8, items: ^[]reply }

// a cluster: keys sharded across servers by consistent hashing
fn cluster_open(addrs: []const net::address, o: cluster_options = ...) (cluster | nomem)
	fn cluster_owner(cl: *const cluster, key: []const u8) usize
	fn cluster_get(cl: *cluster, key, out: *^[]u8) (bool | cluster_failure)
	fn cluster_set(cl: *cluster, key, value, ttl_ms: u64 = 0) (void | cluster_failure)
	fn cluster_remove, cluster_incr, cluster_expire, cluster_push_front,
		cluster_push_back, cluster_set_add, cluster_set_has, cluster_call
type cluster_options = struct { replicas: usize = 1, timeout_ms: u64 = 1000,
	retry_ms: u64 = 1000, password: str = "" }
type cluster_failure = (refused | unavailable | nomem)
lora 
use kv;
use strings;

export fn main() void = {
	let s = kv::open(kv::options { ... })!;
	kv::set_text(&s, "greeting", "hello", kv::set_options { ttl_ms = 60000, ... })!;
	let out: ^[]u8 = [];
	assert(kv::get(&s, "greeting", &out)! is kv::kind);
	assert(strings::from_bytes(out[..]) == "hello");
	assert(kv::incr(&s, "visits")! == 1);
	kv::push_back(&s, "queue", strings::to_bytes("job 1"))!;
	assert(kv::set_add(&s, "tags", strings::to_bytes("fast"))!);
	assert(kv::count(&s) == 4);
	kv::close(&s)!;
}

The store:

  • A shard's keys are in a table of slots holding part of each key's hash and its place in a slab of entries, so a probe seldom reads an entry it does not want, and removing shifts slots back rather than leaving marks.
  • An expired key goes when it is next used, and sweep takes those that are not. With max_memory, a write that needs room evicts the least recently used of five keys sampled (or one at random), or with eviction::refuse is full.
  • A list is two stacks, so both ends push and pop in constant time. A set has an index of its members, as the table has of keys.
  • get fills the buffer it is given, keeping its room: one buffer used for each get allocates only when a value is longer than before.

The log, with dir:

  • Each shard appends every change to its own log, kv-NN.log, and open replays them: a record cut short or damaged, and all after it, are cut off. Each record has its length and a CRC-32. kv.meta keeps the key of the hash and the number of shards, so a key's records stay in one log.
  • sync_policy says when the log is made durable; compact rewrites each log as its shard is now, to a new file renamed over the old.
  • A log is locked while a store has it open: a second store on it is a bad_log. What could not be written is a bad_log too, and no more is written until the store is opened again.
  • With residency::disk, text, bytes and JSON are read from the log when asked for, so a store may hold more than memory does.

Serving and clients:

  • serve gives each connection a coroutine. Requests are RESP arrays of bulk strings or inline commands, pipelined as the client likes, and limited by server_options; one that breaks the protocol or the limits is told why, and its connection closed. The commands are those of strings, numbers, expiry, lists, sets and whole JSON documents (JSON.SET and JSON.GET at $), and KEYS, DBSIZE, FLUSHDB, INFO, SAVE (sync) and BGREWRITEAOF (compact).
  • A client, and a cluster, belong to one coroutine or thread at a time: each makes its own. call sends any command and reads any reply.
  • A cluster puts 160 points for each server on a ring of SipHash-2-4 hashes under a fixed key, so every client places keys alike, and adding a server moves about a fair share of them. A key's value is written to each of its replicas that can be reached and read from the first that can; a server that fails is left alone for retry_ms. Writes are not coordinated: a replica that was down misses what was written meanwhile.

On an M-series Mac, one thread: a get takes about 270 ns with a million keys and 210 ns with ten thousand; an insert about 650 ns, and replacing a value 350 ns. Eight threads on one store, nine gets to a set, do about 11 million operations a second.

deque — growable ring-buffer double-ended queue

deque[T] is a power-of-two circular buffer with O(1) amortized push/pop at both ends and O(1) indexing. Elements must not own heap memory (@owns(T) is rejected).

lora 
let q = deque::new::[int]();
deque::push_back(&q, 1)!;
deque::push_front(&q, 0)!;
assert(deque::pop_front(&q) as int == 0);

heap — binary heap and in-place heapsort

heap[T] provides min-heaps, max-heaps, and custom-comparator priority queues (new_min, new_max, new_by, from_slice_*, push, pop, replace, push_pop, fix, remove) plus in-place heapify_by and heap_sort_by.

lora 
let h = heap::new_min::[int]();
heap::push(&h, 5)!;
heap::push(&h, 1)!;
assert(heap::pop(&h) as int == 1);

btree — ordered B-tree maps and sets

btree::map[K, V] and btree::set[K] provide O(log n) lookup, insert, remove, and zero-allocation in-order / bounded range iteration (range, set_new, set_new_str).

lora 
let m = btree::new::[int, str]();
btree::put(&m, 2, "two")!;
btree::put(&m, 1, "one")!;
let it = btree::range(&m, 1, 2);

ring — fixed-capacity circular buffers and byte_ring

ring[T] and byte_ring pre-allocate a fixed capacity for O(1) non-shifting push/pop, overwrite mode (push_overwrite, bytes_write_overwrite), and bulk wrap-around byte reads/writes (bytes_write, bytes_read, bytes_peek, bytes_find).

lora 
let br = ring::bytes_new(8z)!;
let _ = ring::bytes_write(&br, strings::to_bytes("hello"));

lru — O(1) bounded LRU cache

lru::cache[K, V] combines map::map with an arena doubly-linked list for O(1) get, peek, put (returning updated or evicted values), remove, pop_lru, resize, and MRU-to-LRU for_each.

lora 
let c = lru::new::[str, int](64z, &map::hash_str);
let _ = lru::put(&c, "a", 1)!;
let _ = lru::get(&c, "a");

ascii — zero-table ASCII predicates, case folding, and trimming

Fast byte and string helpers: is_ascii, is_upper, is_lower, is_alpha, is_digit, is_alnum, is_hex, is_space, to_lower, to_upper, eq_ignore_case, cmp_ignore_case, trim_space, and single-allocation to_lower_str / to_upper_str.

bytes — byte-slice utilities and growable buffer

Search, comparison, zero-alloc trimming/splitting (equal, equal_fold, index, index_any, last_index_any, cut, fields, split, replace_all), plus bytes::buffer implementing io::reader, io::writer, and io::byte_reader.

slices — generic slice algorithms and iterators

Generic helpers over []T and []const T: equal, cmp, index_of, contains, starts_with, ends_with, is_sorted, reverse, rotate_left, compact, partition, clone, clone_in, filter, map_to, fold, and zero-alloc chunks / windows.

iter — composable lazy iterators

Defines iter::source[T], range, from_slice, rev_slice, lazy adaptors (take, skip, take_while, skip_while, step_by, filter, map_over, chain, enumerate, zip), and consumers (collect, collect_in, count, fold, find, any, all, nth, last, sum_i64, sum_f64, min_i64, max_i64, product_i64).

glob — full glob matching, gitignore rules, and filesystem walk

Supports *, ?, **, [...] character classes, nested {a,b} brace expansion, compiled glob::pattern, .gitignore-style glob::matcher, and sorted glob::walk.

bitset — dynamic bitset and Bloom filter

Word-packed bitset with range operations (set_range, clear_range), bitwise set algebra (union_with, intersect_with, difference_with, symmetric_difference_with), next_set/next_unset, rank/select, to_bytes, and bloom probabilistic filters.

bitstructs — @bits wire serialization and streaming bit I/O

Provides to_raw, from_raw, put_be, get_be, put_le, get_le, bitfield extract/extract_signed/deposit, and MSB/LSB streaming bit_reader (read_bits, read_bits_signed, peek_bits) and bit_writer.

vectors — SIMD-style lane vectors, matrices, and quaternions

Provides fixed-width lane types (f32x4, f64x2, i32x4, u32x4, u8x16), 2D/3D/4D geometry vectors (vec2, vec3, vec4), 4x4 matrices (mat4, m4_perspective, m4_look_at, m4_inverse), and quat (q_slerp, q_to_mat4, q_rotate_vec3).

decimal — 128-bit exact base-10 arithmetic

Zero-allocation 128-bit base-10 decimal with up to 38 significant digits, @comptime powers-of-10 tables, 6 rounding modes (HALF_EVEN, HALF_UP, HALF_DOWN, FLOOR, CEIL, TRUNC), parse, add/sub/mul/div, rescale, normalize, and encoding::text_encoder/text_decoder.

checksum — fast non-cryptographic checksums and hashes

Includes @comptime slicing-by-8 CRC-32C (crc32c), CRC-64 ECMA-182 and ISO (crc64_ecma, crc64_iso), table-driven CRC-16 CCITT-FALSE and Modbus (crc16_ccitt, crc16_modbus), xxh32 / xxh32_state, xxh64 / xxh64_state, siphash24, siphash13, fletcher16, and fletcher32.

sync — synchronization primitives and typed atomics

Provides typed atomics (atomic_bool, atomic_u64, atomic_i64, atomic_usize, atomic_ptr[T] with fetch_max/fetch_min/bitwise ops), wait_group, once, once_cell[T] (with once_cell_take), writer-preferring rwlock, counting semaphore, cyclic barrier, and countdown latch.

context — cancellation and deadline propagation

Reference-counted cancellation tree (background, with_cancel, with_deadline_ms, with_timeout_ms, with_timeout, with_deadline, cancel, is_cancelled, err, remaining_ms) with iterative cascading cancellation and coroutine-aware wait / wait_ms.

errors — composable error chains and multi-error aggregation

Flat-buffer owned errors::chain (new, from_any, wrap, wrap_str, wrap_any, unwrap, root_cause, contains, format, format_multiline) and errors::multi (multi_new, multi_add, multi_add_chain, multi_add_any, multi_format, join).

env — typed environment lookups, expansion, and .env loader

Provides get, require, has, get_or, get_int, get_u64, get_f64, get_bool, shell-style expand / expand_with ($VAR, ${VAR:-default}, ${VAR-default}, $$), parse_dotenv / load_dotenv, split_list, and OS directory helpers (home_dir, config_dir, cache_dir, data_dir).

cbor — CBOR (RFC 8949) encoder, decoder, and struct codec

Region-backed cbor::parse / cbor::format plus typed marshal / unmarshal supporting @cbor struct tags, integers, floats, byte strings, text strings, arrays, maps, and tags.

toml — TOML 1.0 parser, serializer, and struct codec

Region-backed toml::parse / toml::format and reflection-driven marshal / unmarshal with full TOML 1.0 tables, arrays of tables, inline tables, multi-line strings, and datetimes.

yaml — YAML 1.2 parser, serializer, and struct codec

Region-backed yaml::parse / yaml::parse_all / yaml::format and typed marshal / unmarshal supporting block/flow mappings and sequences, anchors/aliases, merge keys (<<), and block scalars.

sqlite — SQLite3 driver for the sql package

Loads libsqlite3 dynamically via dlopen with zero extra link dependencies for non-SQLite programs; integrates with sql::open, sql::pool, prepared statements, transactions, and last_insert_rowid.

diff — Myers O(ND) slice and line-based unified diffs

Provides generic diff::slices / diff::slices_by, edit_distance, diff::lines, and diff::unified unified diff formatting.

testing — native test, benchmark, and fuzzing framework

Provides testing::t, testing::b, testing::f, reflection-powered assertions (eq, neq, gt, lt, contains, matches, is_err, is_ok, ok), snapshot/golden testing (snapshot), table-driven cases, isolated temp_dir + defer/cleanup, bench_loop / keep, and fuzz_bytes / fuzz_str, integrated with @test, @bench, @fuzz, and lora test.

rt — runtime (used by other modules)

The rt module is the runtime contract: open, close, read, write, malloc/free_, memcpy/memmove/memset, strcmp, exit and the error union. Documented in docs/runtime.md.

mime — MIME types, media parameters, and multipart/form-data

Extension and MIME type lookup, RFC 2045 Content-Type media parameter parsing and formatting, and RFC 2046 / RFC 7578 multipart/form-data reading and writing.

lora 
fn type_by_ext(ext: str) (str | void)
fn type_by_path(path: str) (str | void)
fn ext_by_type(media: str) (str | void)
fn is_text(media: str) bool
fn parse_media_type(s: str) (media_type | bad_media_type | nomem)
fn get_param(m: *const media_type, name: str) (str | void)
fn format_media_type(kind: str, params: []const param_ref) (^str | bad_media_type | nomem)
fn new_multipart_writer() (multipart_writer | nomem)
fn write_field(w: *multipart_writer, name: str, value: str) (void | bad_multipart | nomem)
fn write_file(w: *multipart_writer, field_name: str, filename: str, content_type: str, data: []const u8) (void | bad_multipart | nomem)
fn parse_multipart(body: []const u8, boundary: str) (^[]part | bad_multipart | nomem)
fn part_header(p: *const part, name: str) (str | void)

type_by_ext and ext_by_type perform ASCII case-insensitive lookup across common web, document, image, audio, video, font, and archive types. parse_media_type validates RFC 2045 tokens, lowercases the type/subtype and parameter names, unescapes quoted-string values, and rejects duplicate parameters.

websocket — RFC 6455 WebSocket protocol

Opening handshake key derivation and verification, binary frame encoding/decoding with XOR masking, close status codes, io::reader/io::writer framing, and fragmented message assembly.

lora 
fn generate_key() (^str | nomem)
fn accept_key(client_key: str) (^str | nomem)
fn verify_accept(client_key: str, accept: str) (bool | nomem)
fn encode_frame(out: *^[]u8, op: opcode, payload: []const u8, fin: bool = true, masked: bool = false, mask_key: [4]u8 = [0...]) (void | protocol_error | nomem)
fn decode_frame(data: []const u8, max_payload: usize = 16 * 1024 * 1024, policy: mask_policy = mask_policy::any) ((frame, usize) | incomplete | protocol_error | nomem)
fn read_frame(r: io::reader, max_payload: usize = 16 * 1024 * 1024, policy: mask_policy = mask_policy::any) (frame | done | protocol_error | io::failure | nomem)
fn write_frame(w: io::writer, op: opcode, payload: []const u8, fin: bool = true, masked: bool = false, mask_key: [4]u8 = [0...]) (void | protocol_error | io::failure | nomem)
fn encode_close_frame(out: *^[]u8, code: u16, reason: str = "", masked: bool = false, mask_key: [4]u8 = [0...]) (void | protocol_error | nomem)
fn new_assembler(max_message: usize = 16 * 1024 * 1024) assembler
fn feed_frame(a: *assembler, f: *const frame) (message | void | protocol_error | nomem)
fn reset_assembler(a: *assembler) void

decode_frame and read_frame enforce RFC 6455 invariants: zero RSV bits, valid opcodes, non-fragmented control frames with payloads ≤ 125 bytes, minimal length encodings, and bounded payload sizes. feed_frame reassembles fragmented text/binary messages, passes over interleaved control frames, and validates UTF-8 on completed text messages.

sse — Server-Sent Events (text/event-stream)

Event and comment formatting, io::writer helpers, and a streaming chunked parser following the WHATWG HTML Server-Sent Events specification.

lora

assert(d == 3z);

dotenv — .env file parser and environment loader

Parses # comments, export KEY=VAL, single/double-quoted & multiline values, escape sequences, and $VAR / ${VAR} / ${VAR:-default} expansion (parse, parse_file, get, load_str, load_file).

lora 
let ef = dotenv::parse("PORT=8080\n")!;
assert(dotenv::get(&ef, "PORT") as str == "8080");

ini — INI / .gitconfig-style sectioned config parser and writer

Supports [section] headers, = and : delimiters, ; and # comments, quoted round-tripping, and typed getters (new, parse, parse_file, get, get_int, get_float, get_bool, set, remove, has_section, sections, format).

lora 
let d = ini::parse("[server]\nport = 8080\n")!;
assert(ini::get_int(&d, "server", "port") as i64 == 8080);

qoi — QOI lossless RGB/RGBA image codec

Official QOI specification encoder and decoder with magic, dimension-overflow, and 8-byte end-marker validation (encode, decode, image, SRGB, LINEAR).

lora 
let dec = qoi::decode(qoi_bytes)!;

color — Color parsing, conversions, blending, and WCAG contrast

Hex (#RGB, #RGBA, #RRGGBB, #RRGGBBAA), rgba, hsl, hsv, and oklch conversions, Porter-Duff blend, lerp, lighten, darken, invert, grayscale, WCAG 2.1 contrast_ratio / meets_wcag_aa / meets_wcag_aaa, and 24-bit ansi_fg / ansi_bg.

lora 
let c = color::parse_hex("#ff8040")!;
let cr = color::contrast_ratio(color::rgb(0, 0, 0), color::rgb(255, 255, 255));

msgpack — MessagePack binary encoder and streaming decoder

Compact binary encoder (write_nil, write_bool, write_int, write_uint, write_f32, write_f64, write_str, write_bin, write_array_len, write_map_len, write_ext, bytes, into_bytes) and streaming decoder (new_decoder, peek_kind, read_*, depth-limited skip, remaining, is_eof).

lora 
let enc = msgpack::new_encoder();
defer msgpack::finish_encoder(&enc);
msgpack::write_int(&enc, -42)!;

bitio — Bit-level stream reader and writer

MSB-first and LSB-first bit-stream reader and writer with byte-chunked multi-bit ops and bulk aligned byte transfers (new_reader, read_bit, read_bits, peek_bits, skip_bits, align_byte, read_bytes, new_writer, write_bit, write_bits, writer_align_byte, write_bytes, flush, finish_writer).

lora 
let w = bitio::new_writer(.msb);
defer bitio::finish_writer(&w);
bitio::write_bits(&w, 0b101u64, 3z)!;

dsu — Disjoint-Set Union (Union-Find)

Iterative path-halving and union-by-size disjoint sets (new, make_set, reserve_sets, find, find_const, unite, connected, component_size, component_count, count, reset, finish).

lora 
let uf = dsu::new(5)!;
defer dsu::finish(&uf);
dsu::unite(&uf, 0, 1);
assert(dsu::connected(&uf, 0, 1));

broadcast — Thread-safe 1-to-many broadcast channel

Ring-buffered broadcast bus for OS threads with lag detection (new, subscribe, resubscribe, unsubscribe, send, recv, try_recv, close, is_closed, receiver_count, capacity, len_pending).

lora 
let b = broadcast::new::[int](8)!;
let rx = broadcast::subscribe(&b);
broadcast::send(&b, 42)!;
assert(broadcast::recv(&rx) as int == 42);

interval — Augmented interval tree

Iterative O(log N + K) overlap, point, and containment queries with balanced compaction (new, add, remove, query_point, query_overlap, query_contained, has_overlap, all, compact, count, is_empty, clear, finish).

lora 
let it = interval::new();
defer interval::finish(&it);
interval::add(&it, 10, 20, 1u64)!;
assert(interval::has_overlap(&it, 15, 25)!);
